recent_commits.message: fix(provenance): four surfaces claimed what the call graph did not do
recent_commits.body:
Second, max-effort pass over the v2.4.126 work. The first pass fixed the
reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and
three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in
the code. Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed (2015 baseline + 46 new).

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also
reports pdftotext_path (the exact binary, resolved once and used by the
extraction call sites too, so the receipt cannot name a build that did not
run), pdfminer.six, pypdfium2, opencv, mammoth, beautifulsoup4, lxml --
two of three input formats were unpinned entirely -- plus python_version
and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

recent_commits.body:
MetaESCI asks A-1/A-2. A docpluck SHA did not pin extraction: the same SHA
(a5c02ef) against the same PDF (10.1098/rsos.202336) produced 49,091 vs

get_version_info() reported three keys that were identical in both runs.

pdftotext binary version AND engine (poppler/xpdf differ behaviourally and
share a banner), poppler_version, pdfplumber, camelot, plus the in-repo
sectioning_version and table_extraction_version that were exported and
bumped independently of the package version but never on the receipt.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION is now exported from the package top level.

ExtractionReport carries the same; ExtractionFileResult gains
n_replacement_chars and n_greek_chars (A-2), measured on the normalized
output.

Sibling defects found by sweeping for the same shape:
- NormalizationReport.to_dict() was silently dropping
  column_interleave_pages, a populated field extract_columns documents as
  the canonical source of that signal. Live, predates this change.

  and an elapsed_seconds:0.0 written before the timer stopped.
All three hand-enumerated serializers now derive from asdict().

Also: INBOX_* was missing from .gitignore's cross-project correspondence
block, so an inbox doc had been committed to this public repo (unpushed;
those commits were dropped). Duplicate L-010 heading renumbered.

31 tests, all verified failing against the unfixed code first. Full suite
2046 passed / 0 failed.

recent_commits.body:
ResearchBox hrefs pointing at a specific file within a box were treated as
separate repos; they are now truncated to the box id. The unquoted-filename
capture regexes in code_file_refs() were matching inside already-quoted

basename.

recent_commits.message: Normalize line endings repo-wide with a single text=auto rule
recent_commits.body:
.gitattributes previously forced LF only under tests/testthat/fixtures/,
which also matched binary fixtures there (PDFs, a zip) and forced git to
treat them as text, and left every other CRLF-committed text file (e.g.
data-raw/demo/ground_truth/*.csv, tests/testthat/apis/**/*.html) subject to
each contributor's local core.autocrlf, causing line-ending-only diffs on
checkout.

Replace it with `* text=auto`: git decides text vs. binary from each file's
actual content (the same detection diff/file use), not its extension or
path, so a binary file with a misleading name (e.g. the zip archive stored
as tests/testthat/apis/.../osfstorage-546010.R-FILE) is still handled
correctly with no entry needed, and every genuine text file is stored and
checked out as LF regardless of the checkout platform.

Renormalizes the 23 tracked text files that were actually stored with CRLF
(verified byte-for-byte: only line-ending bytes changed, no content diff).

recent_commits.message: Fix remaining test warnings, including a cross-file llm_use() leak
recent_commits.body:
test-module-power.R's last test block set llm_use(TRUE) and never
reset it, leaking that global option into every test file that ran
afterward in the suite. test-module-repo_check.R and
test-repo-download.R were the two downstream files that triggered
real (unmocked) LLM network calls as a side effect, failing with
connection-refused and printing as warnings even though their actual
assertions still passed. Fixed with withr::defer(llm_use(FALSE)) --
plain on.exit() and withr::local_options() were both tried first and
confirmed, by direct testing, not to restore state correctly through
this project's custom test_that() wrapper in helper.R; withr::defer()
does. Applied the same fix to test-llm.R and test-utils.R, which had
the same unrestored llm_use(TRUE) pattern.

test-archive-zenodo.R and test-repo-download.R had intentional
fake-download-failure scenarios whose warnings were never wrapped in
expect_warning(), the same gap already fixed in
test-archive-dataverse.R -- applied consistently here too.

Full suite: 0 failures, 0 warnings, 4280 passed.

recent_commits.message: Fix R CMD check warnings/notes and cross-test pollution from dead module imports
recent_commits.body:
R CMD check fixes:
- .Rbuildignore: exclude .vscode, .comments, CLAUDE.md; delete stray
  duplicate to_err_is_human.xml at repo root (real copy lives in
  inst/demos/)
- Non-ASCII characters warning: escape functional Unicode (Greek
  statistical notation, math operators, box-drawing table borders, a
  field-separator character, an NBSP constant, a BOM string) as \uXXXX,
  substitute purely decorative comment punctuation with ASCII, across
  12 files
- Undeclared imports warning: add SnowballC, data.table, officer,
  pdftools, readxl, yaml to Suggests (already used via :: throughout)
- Rd cross-references / Rd usage-section warnings: two roxygen blocks
  had drifted onto the wrong function because a plain (non-roxygen)
  comment sat between the doc block and its real target
  (stat_results_long, data_read_head) -- moved each block to the
  correct function; removed one duplicate leftover block; stripped six
  dangling \link{} references to functions that only exist on unmerged
  branches
- R code NOTE: qualify two bare ave() calls as stats::ave(), fix an NSE
  binding in code_setwd(), port the missing .repro_split_args() helper
  r-output.R was calling (only defined on the reproducibility_check
  branch)
- Avoid the "assignments to the global environment" NOTE in
  .r_capture_runner() (a callr subprocess payload, not the user's
  session) by capturing globalenv() into a variable first, which
  R CMD check's static scan does not resolve

Test suite fix:
- Three modules (prereg_check.R, code_check.R, stat_effect_size.R)
  declared roxygen @import for packages (httr, jsonlite, tidyr) they
  never actually use. module_run() require()s every declared @import,
  so running those modules' tests attached httr/jsonlite to the search
  path ahead of metacheck, letting httr::verbose() and
  jsonlite::validate() shadow metacheck::verbose()/validate() for every
  test that ran afterward in the same session -- the reason two
  unrelated test files only failed in full-suite runs, never in
  isolation. Removed the three dead @import lines (a full sweep confirms
  no other module has an unused import).

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: Normalize line endings repo-wide with a single text=auto rule
recent_commits.body:
.gitattributes previously forced LF only under tests/testthat/fixtures/,
which also matched binary fixtures there (PDFs, a zip) and forced git to
treat them as text, and left every other CRLF-committed text file (e.g.
data-raw/demo/ground_truth/*.csv, tests/testthat/apis/**/*.html) subject to
each contributor's local core.autocrlf, causing line-ending-only diffs on
checkout.

Replace it with `* text=auto`: git decides text vs. binary from each file's
actual content (the same detection diff/file use), not its extension or
path, so a binary file with a misleading name (e.g. the zip archive stored
as tests/testthat/apis/.../osfstorage-546010.R-FILE) is still handled
correctly with no entry needed, and every genuine text file is stored and
checked out as LF regardless of the checkout platform.

Renormalizes the 23 tracked text files that were actually stored with CRLF
(verified byte-for-byte: only line-ending bytes changed, no content diff).

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,

ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a fractional `dispersion` in `disperse()`
recent_commits.body:
`dispersion` counts whole units away from `n`, and `n` is a group size.
A fractional step was accepted and then quietly mangled: `n` moved by the
fractional amount while `n_change` was truncated toward zero, so
`disperse(n = 10, dispersion = c(0.5, 1.5))` reported changes of 0 and 1 for
group sizes of 9.5 and 8.5.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Validate `threshold` in `round_up_from()` and `round_down_from()`
recent_commits.body:
`reround()`, `unround()`, and `rounding_offsets()` all route through
`check_threshold_valid()`. The two functions that actually act on `threshold`
did not, so the same invalid argument was an error through one door and silent
nonsense through another: `round_up_from(4.28, 1, threshold = 0)` returned 4.3,
rounding like `round_ceiling()`, and a negative threshold was accepted too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return `NA` from `grim_probability()` where there is nothing to test
recent_commits.body:
A non-positive `n` leaves nothing to test, which `grim()` reports as NA,
but the formula returned 1.03 for n = -3 -- so `grim_map()` displayed a
probability above 1 next to a verdict of NA, stating two incompatible things
about one row. `grim_ratio()` is unchanged; it is documented as the unclamped
one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Ignore undecidable cases in `audit()` summaries
recent_commits.body:
`audit_cols_minimal()` has always counted inconsistencies with
`na.rm = TRUE`, because a case the test could not decide is not an inconsistent
one. The summaries built on top of it did not, so a single missing `n` turned
`mean_grim_prob` -- and `incons_to_prob`, derived from it -- into NA for the
whole table. Same for `mean_x` and `mean_sd` in the DEBIT method.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix `grim_plot()` dropping data, and drop its dead version branch
recent_commits.body:
The axis bounds were scale limits, which discard a tile as soon as one of
its edges falls outside. A mean of 5.00 has a fractional portion of exactly 0,
so its tile reached half its height below the axis and was dropped whole --
`pigs1` contains such a value, so the plot in the package's own examples had
been showing eleven of its twelve value sets. They are coordinate limits now,
which clip instead of discarding.

Negative means are plotted at the fractional portion of their absolute value,
so -2.51 is drawn at 0.51, in the same place as 2.51. GRIM's granularity is
symmetric around zero. Previously such a value fell outside the axis and was
dropped without a word. The new `Negative means` section explains the one
thing the sign still affects: for a one-directional `rounding` method the
raster behind a negative value is the mirrored method's. The tile's color is
unaffected, coming from the `consistency` column.

The blanket `suppressWarnings()` around the final `print()` is gone; it had
hidden both of the above. `show_raster = FALSE` works again -- the plot object
was only created inside the branch that draws the raster, so the documented
argument failed with "object 'p' not found". A zero-row `data` is now an
explained error instead of R's "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed".

The data is drawn by one `geom_tile()` call using `linewidth`. There were two,
chosen at run time on `utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.4"`; DESCRIPTION
has required ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0) ever since, so the `size` branch was
unreachable and its deprecation warning was being suppressed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix DEBIT's false alarm at a reported mean of 0.50
recent_commits.body:
`debit_scalar()` reconstructed the SD at the two bounds of the mean's
rounding interval and concluded that every SD in between was reachable. That is
an intermediate-value argument and it needs monotonicity, which
`sd_binary_mean_n()` does not have: it is a downward parabola peaking at a mean
of 0.5. An interval containing 0.5 reaches SDs above both endpoints, and for a
mean of exactly 0.50 the interval is symmetric around the peak, so both
endpoints give the same SD and the attainable band collapsed to a point.
`debit(x = 0.50, sd = 0.503, n = 100, digits_x = 2, digits_sd = 3)` was FALSE
for 50 ones and 50 zeros. The peak is now evaluated too. The error only ever
turned TRUE into FALSE, so nothing that used to pass now fails.

Also rejects a `formula` other than "mean_n" with the package's own error. The
others need a group size DEBIT is not given, so they reached
`reconstruct_sd()` and failed with R's "argument \"group_0\" is missing",
about an argument the user never saw.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve sequence-mapper dispersion limits per variable
recent_commits.body:
`out_min = "auto"` meant one decimal unit above zero for every dispersed
variable, though it was written for `n`. For a negative reported mean it
removed the whole lower half of the sequence, and 0 -- a legal mean, SD, and
proportion -- was out of reach everywhere. `function_map_seq()` gains
`.var_bounds`, and "auto" now resolves through it per variable: `n` keeps a
floor of 1 whether declared or not, GRIMMER's `sd` gets 0, DEBIT's `x` and
`sd` get [0, 1], and a mean is unbounded. `.out_max` defaults to "auto" for
the same reason. This also fixes `debit_map_seq()` failing outright whenever a
reported value sat close enough to 0 or 1 for the dispersion to cross it.

`reverse_map_seq()` no longer infers the reported value from the shape of the
sequence -- the midpoint of its gap, or its median if it had none. That is only
valid for a complete sequence: once a limit had truncated one side, the gap
disappeared and the median branch returned a plausible wrong number, so
`audit_seq()` on a reported mean of -2.51 gave -2.48 and the opposite verdict.
The value now comes from the `diff_var` column, which records how many steps
each row sits from it. `index_case_interpolate()` is replaced by
`index_case_from_diff()`, which errors rather than guessing when a group's
rows disagree.

The "no inconsistent cases" warning now always names `include_consistent`. It
named the R argument only when `interactive()` was TRUE and otherwise told the
user to untick a checkbox in the Shiny app -- so scripts, R Markdown, and test
runs got the checkbox message.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop zero steps in `seq_disperse()`'s `dispersion`
recent_commits.body:
A value in `dispersion` is a number of steps taken both up and down from
`from`, so a step of 0 is `from` itself, once in each direction. Whether
`from` belongs in its own sequence is what `include_reported` decides, so a
zero step added it two more times: `seq_disperse(4.02, dispersion = 0)` was
three copies of "4.02", and `grim_map_seq(dispersion = c(0, 1, 2))` returned
the reported case twice, which `audit_seq()` counted twice.

Also documents what `out_min = "auto"` suits and what to pass instead. It
resolves to one decimal unit above zero, which is right for a count and wrong
for anything that can reach zero or go negative.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Normalize line endings repo-wide with a single text=auto rule
recent_commits.body:
.gitattributes previously forced LF only under tests/testthat/fixtures/,
which also matched binary fixtures there (PDFs, a zip) and forced git to
treat them as text, and left every other CRLF-committed text file (e.g.
data-raw/demo/ground_truth/*.csv, tests/testthat/apis/**/*.html) subject to
each contributor's local core.autocrlf, causing line-ending-only diffs on
checkout.

Replace it with `* text=auto`: git decides text vs. binary from each file's
actual content (the same detection diff/file use), not its extension or
path, so a binary file with a misleading name (e.g. the zip archive stored
as tests/testthat/apis/.../osfstorage-546010.R-FILE) is still handled
correctly with no entry needed, and every genuine text file is stored and
checked out as LF regardless of the checkout platform.

Renormalizes the 23 tracked text files that were actually stored with CRLF
(verified byte-for-byte: only line-ending bytes changed, no content diff).

recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

than dropped:

                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.

  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite

(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

recent_commits.message: Normalize line endings repo-wide with a single text=auto rule
recent_commits.body:
.gitattributes previously forced LF only under tests/testthat/fixtures/,
which also matched binary fixtures there (PDFs, a zip) and forced git to
treat them as text, and left every other CRLF-committed text file (e.g.
data-raw/demo/ground_truth/*.csv, tests/testthat/apis/**/*.html) subject to
each contributor's local core.autocrlf, causing line-ending-only diffs on
checkout.

Replace it with `* text=auto`: git decides text vs. binary from each file's
actual content (the same detection diff/file use), not its extension or
path, so a binary file with a misleading name (e.g. the zip archive stored
as tests/testthat/apis/.../osfstorage-546010.R-FILE) is still handled
correctly with no entry needed, and every genuine text file is stored and
checked out as LF regardless of the checkout platform.

Renormalizes the 23 tracked text files that were actually stored with CRLF
(verified byte-for-byte: only line-ending bytes changed, no content diff).

recent_commits.message: Fix remaining test warnings, including a cross-file llm_use() leak
recent_commits.body:
test-module-power.R's last test block set llm_use(TRUE) and never
reset it, leaking that global option into every test file that ran
afterward in the suite. test-module-repo_check.R and
test-repo-download.R were the two downstream files that triggered
real (unmocked) LLM network calls as a side effect, failing with
connection-refused and printing as warnings even though their actual
assertions still passed. Fixed with withr::defer(llm_use(FALSE)) --
plain on.exit() and withr::local_options() were both tried first and
confirmed, by direct testing, not to restore state correctly through
this project's custom test_that() wrapper in helper.R; withr::defer()
does. Applied the same fix to test-llm.R and test-utils.R, which had
the same unrestored llm_use(TRUE) pattern.

test-archive-zenodo.R and test-repo-download.R had intentional
fake-download-failure scenarios whose warnings were never wrapped in
expect_warning(), the same gap already fixed in
test-archive-dataverse.R -- applied consistently here too.

Full suite: 0 failures, 0 warnings, 4280 passed.

- .Rbuildignore: exclude .vscode, .comments, CLAUDE.md; delete stray
  duplicate to_err_is_human.xml at repo root (real copy lives in
  inst/demos/)
- Non-ASCII characters warning: escape functional Unicode (Greek

  substitute purely decorative comment punctuation with ASCII, across
  12 files
- Undeclared imports warning: add SnowballC, data.table, officer,

- Rd cross-references / Rd usage-section warnings: two roxygen blocks
  had drifted onto the wrong function because a plain (non-roxygen)
  comment sat between the doc block and its real target
  (stat_results_long, data_read_head) -- moved each block to the
  correct function; removed one duplicate leftover block; stripped six
  dangling \link{} references to functions that only exist on unmerged
  branches
- R code NOTE: qualify two bare ave() calls as stats::ave(), fix an NSE
  binding in code_setwd(), port the missing .repro_split_args() helper
  r-output.R was calling (only defined on the reproducibility_check
  branch)
- Avoid the "assignments to the global environment" NOTE in
  .r_capture_runner() (a callr subprocess payload, not the user's
  session) by capturing globalenv() into a variable first, which
  R CMD check's static scan does not resolve

Test suite fix:
- Three modules (prereg_check.R, code_check.R, stat_effect_size.R)
  declared roxygen @import for packages (httr, jsonlite, tidyr) they
  never actually use. module_run() require()s every declared @import,
  so running those modules' tests attached httr/jsonlite to the search
  path ahead of metacheck, letting httr::verbose() and
  jsonlite::validate() shadow metacheck::verbose()/validate() for every
  test that ran afterward in the same session -- the reason two
  unrelated test files only failed in full-suite runs, never in
  isolation. Removed the three dead @import lines (a full sweep confirms
  no other module has an unused import).

recent_commits.message: Fix .gitattributes marking binary fixtures as text, causing CRLF corruption
recent_commits.body:
pdf/zip/omv/jasp fixture files under tests/testthat/fixtures/ were matched
by a blanket "text eol=lf" rule intended for text fixtures. Because these
formats are binary, Git rewrote \r\n/\n byte sequences inside their actual
data on every checkout where core.autocrlf differs from the stored blob's
line endings, producing "modified" diffs with no real content change and
breaking fixture file_hash comparisons (md5sum of the raw bytes) in tests.

Replaced the fixtures-only rule with a repo-wide "* text=auto", which lets
Git classify each file as text or binary by inspecting its content, so new
files stay correctly classified without needing an extension list kept up
to date by hand. Added explicit "-text" overrides only for the formats
that must never be touched even if content-sniffing were to misjudge them:
pdf and zip are unambiguous binary; omv and jasp are Java/ZIP archives
despite their extension.

Renormalized the index with `git add --renormalize .`, which surfaced and
fixed pre-existing CRLF drift in unrelated CSV/HTML/XML/R files that had
never been covered by any .gitattributes rule (line-ending-only changes,
verified with `git diff -w` showing no content difference).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix logpath() returning character(0) when no log file exists yet
recent_commits.body:
logpath() created a new log file on disk but never updated the log
variable it returns, so it kept returning the stale character(0)
from list.files(). This made logger()'s file.exists(logpath) check
error with "argument is of length zero" on any machine without a
pre-existing log file, which is why R CMD check failed on every
r-universe build platform (the lastlog()/logger() example runs in a
clean environment with no log yet).

recent_commits.message: Reject a fractional `dispersion` in `disperse()`
recent_commits.body:
`dispersion` counts whole units away from `n`, and `n` is a group size.
A fractional step was accepted and then quietly mangled: `n` moved by the
fractional amount while `n_change` was truncated toward zero, so
`disperse(n = 10, dispersion = c(0.5, 1.5))` reported changes of 0 and 1 for
group sizes of 9.5 and 8.5.

recent_commits.body:
`reround()`, `unround()`, and `rounding_offsets()` all route through
`check_threshold_valid()`. The two functions that actually act on `threshold`
did not, so the same invalid argument was an error through one door and silent
nonsense through another: `round_up_from(4.28, 1, threshold = 0)` returned 4.3,
rounding like `round_ceiling()`, and a negative threshold was accepted too.

recent_commits.message: Ignore undecidable cases in `audit()` summaries
recent_commits.body:
`audit_cols_minimal()` has always counted inconsistencies with
`na.rm = TRUE`, because a case the test could not decide is not an inconsistent
one. The summaries built on top of it did not, so a single missing `n` turned
`mean_grim_prob` -- and `incons_to_prob`, derived from it -- into NA for the
whole table. Same for `mean_x` and `mean_sd` in the DEBIT method.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix `grim_plot()` dropping data, and drop its dead version branch
recent_commits.body:
The axis bounds were scale limits, which discard a tile as soon as one of
its edges falls outside. A mean of 5.00 has a fractional portion of exactly 0,
so its tile reached half its height below the axis and was dropped whole --
`pigs1` contains such a value, so the plot in the package's own examples had
been showing eleven of its twelve value sets. They are coordinate limits now,
which clip instead of discarding.

Negative means are plotted at the fractional portion of their absolute value,
so -2.51 is drawn at 0.51, in the same place as 2.51. GRIM's granularity is
symmetric around zero. Previously such a value fell outside the axis and was
dropped without a word. The new `Negative means` section explains the one
thing the sign still affects: for a one-directional `rounding` method the
raster behind a negative value is the mirrored method's. The tile's color is
unaffected, coming from the `consistency` column.

The blanket `suppressWarnings()` around the final `print()` is gone; it had
hidden both of the above. `show_raster = FALSE` works again -- the plot object
was only created inside the branch that draws the raster, so the documented
argument failed with "object 'p' not found". A zero-row `data` is now an
explained error instead of R's "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed".

The data is drawn by one `geom_tile()` call using `linewidth`. There were two,
chosen at run time on `utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.4"`; DESCRIPTION
has required ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0) ever since, so the `size` branch was
unreachable and its deprecation warning was being suppressed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix DEBIT's false alarm at a reported mean of 0.50
recent_commits.body:
`debit_scalar()` reconstructed the SD at the two bounds of the mean's
rounding interval and concluded that every SD in between was reachable. That is
an intermediate-value argument and it needs monotonicity, which
`sd_binary_mean_n()` does not have: it is a downward parabola peaking at a mean
of 0.5. An interval containing 0.5 reaches SDs above both endpoints, and for a
mean of exactly 0.50 the interval is symmetric around the peak, so both
endpoints give the same SD and the attainable band collapsed to a point.
`debit(x = 0.50, sd = 0.503, n = 100, digits_x = 2, digits_sd = 3)` was FALSE
for 50 ones and 50 zeros. The peak is now evaluated too. The error only ever
turned TRUE into FALSE, so nothing that used to pass now fails.

Also rejects a `formula` other than "mean_n" with the package's own error. The
others need a group size DEBIT is not given, so they reached
`reconstruct_sd()` and failed with R's "argument \"group_0\" is missing",
about an argument the user never saw.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve sequence-mapper dispersion limits per variable
recent_commits.body:
`out_min = "auto"` meant one decimal unit above zero for every dispersed
variable, though it was written for `n`. For a negative reported mean it
removed the whole lower half of the sequence, and 0 -- a legal mean, SD, and
proportion -- was out of reach everywhere. `function_map_seq()` gains
`.var_bounds`, and "auto" now resolves through it per variable: `n` keeps a
floor of 1 whether declared or not, GRIMMER's `sd` gets 0, DEBIT's `x` and
`sd` get [0, 1], and a mean is unbounded. `.out_max` defaults to "auto" for
the same reason. This also fixes `debit_map_seq()` failing outright whenever a
reported value sat close enough to 0 or 1 for the dispersion to cross it.

`reverse_map_seq()` no longer infers the reported value from the shape of the
sequence -- the midpoint of its gap, or its median if it had none. That is only
valid for a complete sequence: once a limit had truncated one side, the gap
disappeared and the median branch returned a plausible wrong number, so
`audit_seq()` on a reported mean of -2.51 gave -2.48 and the opposite verdict.
The value now comes from the `diff_var` column, which records how many steps
each row sits from it. `index_case_interpolate()` is replaced by
`index_case_from_diff()`, which errors rather than guessing when a group's
rows disagree.

The "no inconsistent cases" warning now always names `include_consistent`. It
named the R argument only when `interactive()` was TRUE and otherwise told the
user to untick a checkbox in the Shiny app -- so scripts, R Markdown, and test
runs got the checkbox message.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop zero steps in `seq_disperse()`'s `dispersion`
recent_commits.body:
A value in `dispersion` is a number of steps taken both up and down from
`from`, so a step of 0 is `from` itself, once in each direction. Whether
`from` belongs in its own sequence is what `include_reported` decides, so a
zero step added it two more times: `seq_disperse(4.02, dispersion = 0)` was
three copies of "4.02", and `grim_map_seq(dispersion = c(0, 1, 2))` returned
the reported case twice, which `audit_seq()` counted twice.

Also documents what `out_min = "auto"` suits and what to pass instead. It
resolves to one decimal unit above zero, which is right for a count and wrong
for anything that can reach zero or go negative.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: Return zero rows from `unround()` for zero-length input
recent_commits.body:
Recycling stops at zero. Taking the maximum of all argument lengths ignored
an empty argument and let the length-1 defaults set the row count, so
`unround(character(0))` returned one row of missing values.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a fractional `dispersion` in `disperse()`
recent_commits.body:
`dispersion` counts whole units away from `n`, and `n` is a group size.
A fractional step was accepted and then quietly mangled: `n` moved by the
fractional amount while `n_change` was truncated toward zero, so
`disperse(n = 10, dispersion = c(0.5, 1.5))` reported changes of 0 and 1 for
group sizes of 9.5 and 8.5.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Validate `threshold` in `round_up_from()` and `round_down_from()`
recent_commits.body:
`reround()`, `unround()`, and `rounding_offsets()` all route through
`check_threshold_valid()`. The two functions that actually act on `threshold`
did not, so the same invalid argument was an error through one door and silent
nonsense through another: `round_up_from(4.28, 1, threshold = 0)` returned 4.3,
rounding like `round_ceiling()`, and a negative threshold was accepted too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return `NA` from `grim_probability()` where there is nothing to test
recent_commits.body:
A non-positive `n` leaves nothing to test, which `grim()` reports as NA,
but the formula returned 1.03 for n = -3 -- so `grim_map()` displayed a
probability above 1 next to a verdict of NA, stating two incompatible things
about one row. `grim_ratio()` is unchanged; it is documented as the unclamped
one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Ignore undecidable cases in `audit()` summaries
recent_commits.body:
`audit_cols_minimal()` has always counted inconsistencies with
`na.rm = TRUE`, because a case the test could not decide is not an inconsistent
one. The summaries built on top of it did not, so a single missing `n` turned
`mean_grim_prob` -- and `incons_to_prob`, derived from it -- into NA for the
whole table. Same for `mean_x` and `mean_sd` in the DEBIT method.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix `grim_plot()` dropping data, and drop its dead version branch
recent_commits.body:
The axis bounds were scale limits, which discard a tile as soon as one of
its edges falls outside. A mean of 5.00 has a fractional portion of exactly 0,
so its tile reached half its height below the axis and was dropped whole --
`pigs1` contains such a value, so the plot in the package's own examples had
been showing eleven of its twelve value sets. They are coordinate limits now,
which clip instead of discarding.

Negative means are plotted at the fractional portion of their absolute value,
so -2.51 is drawn at 0.51, in the same place as 2.51. GRIM's granularity is
symmetric around zero. Previously such a value fell outside the axis and was
dropped without a word. The new `Negative means` section explains the one
thing the sign still affects: for a one-directional `rounding` method the
raster behind a negative value is the mirrored method's. The tile's color is
unaffected, coming from the `consistency` column.

The blanket `suppressWarnings()` around the final `print()` is gone; it had
hidden both of the above. `show_raster = FALSE` works again -- the plot object
was only created inside the branch that draws the raster, so the documented
argument failed with "object 'p' not found". A zero-row `data` is now an
explained error instead of R's "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed".

The data is drawn by one `geom_tile()` call using `linewidth`. There were two,
chosen at run time on `utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.4"`; DESCRIPTION
has required ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0) ever since, so the `size` branch was
unreachable and its deprecation warning was being suppressed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix DEBIT's false alarm at a reported mean of 0.50
recent_commits.body:
`debit_scalar()` reconstructed the SD at the two bounds of the mean's
rounding interval and concluded that every SD in between was reachable. That is
an intermediate-value argument and it needs monotonicity, which
`sd_binary_mean_n()` does not have: it is a downward parabola peaking at a mean
of 0.5. An interval containing 0.5 reaches SDs above both endpoints, and for a
mean of exactly 0.50 the interval is symmetric around the peak, so both
endpoints give the same SD and the attainable band collapsed to a point.
`debit(x = 0.50, sd = 0.503, n = 100, digits_x = 2, digits_sd = 3)` was FALSE
for 50 ones and 50 zeros. The peak is now evaluated too. The error only ever
turned TRUE into FALSE, so nothing that used to pass now fails.

Also rejects a `formula` other than "mean_n" with the package's own error. The
others need a group size DEBIT is not given, so they reached
`reconstruct_sd()` and failed with R's "argument \"group_0\" is missing",
about an argument the user never saw.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve sequence-mapper dispersion limits per variable
recent_commits.body:
`out_min = "auto"` meant one decimal unit above zero for every dispersed
variable, though it was written for `n`. For a negative reported mean it
removed the whole lower half of the sequence, and 0 -- a legal mean, SD, and
proportion -- was out of reach everywhere. `function_map_seq()` gains
`.var_bounds`, and "auto" now resolves through it per variable: `n` keeps a
floor of 1 whether declared or not, GRIMMER's `sd` gets 0, DEBIT's `x` and
`sd` get [0, 1], and a mean is unbounded. `.out_max` defaults to "auto" for
the same reason. This also fixes `debit_map_seq()` failing outright whenever a
reported value sat close enough to 0 or 1 for the dispersion to cross it.

`reverse_map_seq()` no longer infers the reported value from the shape of the
sequence -- the midpoint of its gap, or its median if it had none. That is only
valid for a complete sequence: once a limit had truncated one side, the gap
disappeared and the median branch returned a plausible wrong number, so
`audit_seq()` on a reported mean of -2.51 gave -2.48 and the opposite verdict.
The value now comes from the `diff_var` column, which records how many steps
each row sits from it. `index_case_interpolate()` is replaced by
`index_case_from_diff()`, which errors rather than guessing when a group's
rows disagree.

The "no inconsistent cases" warning now always names `include_consistent`. It
named the R argument only when `interactive()` was TRUE and otherwise told the
user to untick a checkbox in the Shiny app -- so scripts, R Markdown, and test
runs got the checkbox message.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop zero steps in `seq_disperse()`'s `dispersion`
recent_commits.body:
A value in `dispersion` is a number of steps taken both up and down from
`from`, so a step of 0 is `from` itself, once in each direction. Whether
`from` belongs in its own sequence is what `include_reported` decides, so a
zero step added it two more times: `seq_disperse(4.02, dispersion = 0)` was
three copies of "4.02", and `grim_map_seq(dispersion = c(0, 1, 2))` returned
the reported case twice, which `audit_seq()` counted twice.

Also documents what `out_min = "auto"` suits and what to pass instead. It
resolves to one decimal unit above zero, which is right for a count and wrong
for anything that can reach zero or go negative.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix .gitattributes marking binary fixtures as text, causing CRLF corruption
recent_commits.body:
pdf/zip/omv/jasp fixture files under tests/testthat/fixtures/ were matched
by a blanket "text eol=lf" rule intended for text fixtures. Because these
formats are binary, Git rewrote \r\n/\n byte sequences inside their actual
data on every checkout where core.autocrlf differs from the stored blob's
line endings, producing "modified" diffs with no real content change and
breaking fixture file_hash comparisons (md5sum of the raw bytes) in tests.

Replaced the fixtures-only rule with a repo-wide "* text=auto", which lets
Git classify each file as text or binary by inspecting its content, so new
files stay correctly classified without needing an extension list kept up
to date by hand. Added explicit "-text" overrides only for the formats
that must never be touched even if content-sniffing were to misjudge them:
pdf and zip are unambiguous binary; omv and jasp are Java/ZIP archives
despite their extension.

Renormalized the index with `git add --renormalize .`, which surfaced and
fixed pre-existing CRLF drift in unrelated CSV/HTML/XML/R files that had
never been covered by any .gitattributes rule (line-ending-only changes,
verified with `git diff -w` showing no content difference).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix logpath() returning character(0) when no log file exists yet
recent_commits.body:
logpath() created a new log file on disk but never updated the log
variable it returns, so it kept returning the stale character(0)
from list.files(). This made logger()'s file.exists(logpath) check
error with "argument is of length zero" on any machine without a
pre-existing log file, which is why R CMD check failed on every
r-universe build platform (the lastlog()/logger() example runs in a
clean environment with no log yet).

recent_commits.body:
logpath() created a new log file on disk but never updated the log
variable it returns, so it kept returning the stale character(0)
from list.files(). This made logger()'s file.exists(logpath) check
error with "argument is of length zero" on any machine without a
pre-existing log file, which is why R CMD check failed on every
r-universe build platform (the lastlog()/logger() example runs in a
clean environment with no log yet).

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): snapshot suite resolved fixtures under the pre-2026-08-03 Vibe root
recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12
byte-for-byte extraction tests SKIPPED — silently, reporting green.

Before: 24 skipped in 0.17s.  After: 25 passed in 201.80s.

This is verbatim the failure the portfolio hard rule warns about ("a discovery
helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a
clean one" — the same rule notes the 2026-08-03 move went unnoticed for five
weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,
and a new test_fixture_root_exists FAILS when the root is absent. A missing
individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): restore the corpus render gate, dead since the 2026-08-06 redaction
recent_commits.body:
`SPIKE_OUT_DIRS` held two identical literals reading "an internal design
doc". The de-referencing pass replaced the two real baseline paths with that
placeholder prose, so every run since printed "ERROR: no spike baselines
found" and exited 1 — while docpluck-qa check 7b documents that exact message
as an expected clean skip on a fresh checkout. A CRITICAL render-regression
gate was disabled for a week and its deadness read as normal. The 26 baseline
files (7 + 19, the documented count) were on disk the whole time.

Resolved via DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR with a runtime default. Missing
fixture is now a loud SKIP (exit 0); baseline dirs that exist but hold no .md
is a FAIL (exit 1). Conflating those two is what trained people to ignore the
message — the same SKIP-vs-ERROR confusion already fixed once in
tests/test_canary_provenance.py.

Restored and run: 26 / 26 PASS at v2.4.126, so this release introduces no
render regression.

reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and

moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

recent_commits.message: Fix .gitattributes marking binary fixtures as text, causing CRLF corruption
recent_commits.body:
pdf/zip/omv/jasp fixture files under tests/testthat/fixtures/ were matched
by a blanket "text eol=lf" rule intended for text fixtures. Because these
formats are binary, Git rewrote \r\n/\n byte sequences inside their actual
data on every checkout where core.autocrlf differs from the stored blob's
line endings, producing "modified" diffs with no real content change and
breaking fixture file_hash comparisons (md5sum of the raw bytes) in tests.

Replaced the fixtures-only rule with a repo-wide "* text=auto", which lets
Git classify each file as text or binary by inspecting its content, so new
files stay correctly classified without needing an extension list kept up
to date by hand. Added explicit "-text" overrides only for the formats
that must never be touched even if content-sniffing were to misjudge them:
pdf and zip are unambiguous binary; omv and jasp are Java/ZIP archives
despite their extension.

Renormalized the index with `git add --renormalize .`, which surfaced and
fixed pre-existing CRLF drift in unrelated CSV/HTML/XML/R files that had
never been covered by any .gitattributes rule (line-ending-only changes,
verified with `git diff -w` showing no content difference).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

converts a repository's raw trial-level data into Behaverse-format
paradata, using read_iqx() (R/iqx.R) to name otherwise-opaque Inquisit
tasks from their .iqx script content.

convert_codebook() (R/codebook-convert.R) is the labelled-data-frame
companion to convert_psychds(): built from the same data_check /
codebook_check outputs, it prepares input for the codebook package's
rich HTML output without metacheck taking on rmarkdown/pandoc/codebook
as hard dependencies.

scale_items, scale_meta, and scale_scoring (R/scale_items.R,
data-raw/) are the item-level companions to the existing `scales`
table: one row per instrument's items, subscales, reverse-keyed items
and reliabilities, harvested from the OpenScales .osd definitions.

recent_commits.message: Add convert_psychds: write a Psych-DS/RO-Crate release from a paper's data
recent_commits.body:
convert_psychds() (R/psychds-convert.R) is the file-writing counterpart
to the psychds_check module: the check reports the compliance gap to
the Psych-DS standard, this builds a compliant copy on disk (RO-Crate
metadata, dataset_description.json per study, converted data files,
requirements.txt from the code's declared packages). psychds-validate.R
adds a native validator to confirm the output is actually compliant.

Depends on inst/modules/psychds_check.R for the file-to-target plan;
that file is duplicated here and on the reproducibility_check branch
rather than kept in one shared place, since neither module needs the
other's code or disk output (convert_psychds only optionally reads a
reproducibility_check result if one is already in the module chain,
it never calls into reproducibility_check's code). See the NOTE at
both modules' call sites for the planned extraction once both are
mature.

Also carries the report.R change that lets a captured module-chain
result be reused without re-reading the paper, which convert_psychds
relies on.

Ported from the data_check branch.

recent_commits.message: Add reproducibility_check: run a paper's code against its data
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check() (R/reproducibility_check.R,
R/reproducibility_check_docker.R, inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R)
assesses whether a paper's code can run on its data. Static analysis
(dependencies, run order, missing inputs) always runs; execute = TRUE
additionally runs the code in an isolated callr subprocess or a
locked-down Docker container.

Depends on inst/modules/psychds_check.R for the file-to-target plan
used to rewrite each script's data paths and materialise a throwaway
run directory; that file is duplicated here and on the convert_psychds
branch rather than kept in one shared place, since neither module
needs the other's code or disk output. See the NOTE at both modules'
call sites for the planned extraction once both are mature.

Also carries the JASP/jamovi table-reading and reported-vs-output
matching changes this module calls directly (stat-output.R,
stat-tables.R, stato-map.R, mplus.R, stata.R, spv.R, extract-tests.R,
match-table.R, match-reported.R), and the report.R change that lets a
captured module-chain result be reused without re-reading the paper.

Ported from the data_check branch.
