recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): snapshot suite resolved fixtures under the pre-2026-08-03 Vibe root
recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12
byte-for-byte extraction tests SKIPPED — silently, reporting green.

Before: 24 skipped in 0.17s.  After: 25 passed in 201.80s.

This is verbatim the failure the portfolio hard rule warns about ("a discovery
helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a
clean one" — the same rule notes the 2026-08-03 move went unnoticed for five
weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,
and a new test_fixture_root_exists FAILS when the root is absent. A missing
individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): restore the corpus render gate, dead since the 2026-08-06 redaction
recent_commits.body:
`SPIKE_OUT_DIRS` held two identical literals reading "an internal design
doc". The de-referencing pass replaced the two real baseline paths with that
placeholder prose, so every run since printed "ERROR: no spike baselines
found" and exited 1 — while docpluck-qa check 7b documents that exact message
as an expected clean skip on a fresh checkout. A CRITICAL render-regression
gate was disabled for a week and its deadness read as normal. The 26 baseline

Resolved via DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR with a runtime default. Missing
fixture is now a loud SKIP (exit 0); baseline dirs that exist but hold no .md
is a FAIL (exit 1). Conflating those two is what trained people to ignore the
message — the same SKIP-vs-ERROR confusion already fixed once in
tests/test_canary_provenance.py.

render regression.

An independent pass re-derived all eight behavioural claims in fresh
processes against a real paper (identical version dict before vs after
importing every engine; 245ms/16ms; byte-identical default render at
21776 chars vs standard 21777 and none 22487; 12/12 CLI sections carrying
subheadings; zero bare "pdftotext" literals). All eight held. It also found
what follows.

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_v2.4.126.md contained a FALSE claim: "both consumer
surfaces now derive from the dataclass" was true of the library CLI and
false of the service, which still hand-enumerated nine keys and still
dropped `subheadings`. Fixed the data loss rather than only the sentence —

can emit it against the CURRENT 2.4.125 pin; the switch to Section.to_dict()

  docpluck.sections first in a fresh process resolves).
- an unused import in the test module.

INSPECTED rather than deleted (an assigned-but-unused value in extraction
logic is the "silently dropped computed value" class — all three were
vestigial, none was a lost value), one dead local in SectionedDocument.all()

reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and
three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in
the code. Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed (2015 baseline + 46 new).

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also
reports pdftotext_path (the exact binary, resolved once and used by the
extraction call sites too, so the receipt cannot name a build that did not
run), pdfminer.six, pypdfium2, opencv, mammoth, beautifulsoup4, lxml --
two of three input formats were unpinned entirely -- plus python_version
and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),

recent_commits.message: Add an OSF download app, extend the report app, and fix several bugs
recent_commits.body:
New osf_app(): enter an OSF user or project ID, search and tick the projects
you want, then download them. Run locally, metacheck downloads the files onto
your computer. Hosted, the browser fetches each archive straight from
files.osf.io and saves it, so the server never stores or relays project files.
The OSF permits this cross-origin, but only for requests carrying an
Authorization header, so one is always sent (a placeholder when the visitor
has no token).

report_app(): data_check and codebook_check now run alongside repo_check and
code_check, grouped as repo_modules so the four cannot drift apart.

Bug fixes:
* The report run read input$create_crossref, which no input ever set, so
  CrossRef was never queried whatever the checkbox said. It is query_crossref.
* A Windows path put a backslash-U sequence into the displayed R code, which
  R cannot parse, so the code shown could not be run.
* The shown R code did not drop ref_accuracy when CrossRef was off, unlike
  the run it claimed to reproduce.
* The OSF token was stored by an observer with ignoreInit = TRUE, which
  discarded the first token typed, so private projects always failed.
* A download into a folder that cannot be written to (C:/ without
  administrator rights) is now refused with a message about saving rather
  than reported as a download failure.

Both apps keep anonymous usage statistics (sessions, downloads or reports, and
sizes) to support future grant applications. No identifier of any kind is
recorded and nothing is sent anywhere; only the hosted apps count.

data_check: the file tree is drawn as a tree again rather than a paginated
table, keeping the type icons, study and naming columns.

recent_commits.message: Count decimal places correctly in scientific notation
recent_commits.body:
R writes 0.0001 as "1e-04", so the digits after the decimal point are
not the decimal places of the number. decimal_places_scalar() sets the
step size in seq_disperse(), seq_endpoint(), and seq_distance(), all of
which were silently wrong below 0.001.

recent_commits.message: Fix DEBIT at means of exactly 0 and 1
recent_commits.body:
The mean's rounding bounds reach outside the range that a mean of binary
data can occupy, where the SD is undefined, so the verdict came out NA
for a mean reported as 0.00 or 1.00 -- both of which are consistent.
Clamp the bounds to that range, and clamp a negative SD lower bound to
zero as grimmer_scalar() already does.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): snapshot suite resolved fixtures under the pre-2026-08-03 Vibe root
recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12
byte-for-byte extraction tests SKIPPED — silently, reporting green.

Before: 24 skipped in 0.17s.  After: 25 passed in 201.80s.

This is verbatim the failure the portfolio hard rule warns about ("a discovery
helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a
clean one" — the same rule notes the 2026-08-03 move went unnoticed for five
weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,
and a new test_fixture_root_exists FAILS when the root is absent. A missing
individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): restore the corpus render gate, dead since the 2026-08-06 redaction
recent_commits.body:
`SPIKE_OUT_DIRS` held two identical literals reading "an internal design
doc". The de-referencing pass replaced the two real baseline paths with that
placeholder prose, so every run since printed "ERROR: no spike baselines
found" and exited 1 — while docpluck-qa check 7b documents that exact message
as an expected clean skip on a fresh checkout. A CRITICAL render-regression
gate was disabled for a week and its deadness read as normal. The 26 baseline
files (7 + 19, the documented count) were on disk the whole time.

Resolved via DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR with a runtime default. Missing
fixture is now a loud SKIP (exit 0); baseline dirs that exist but hold no .md
is a FAIL (exit 1). Conflating those two is what trained people to ignore the
message — the same SKIP-vs-ERROR confusion already fixed once in
tests/test_canary_provenance.py.

Restored and run: 26 / 26 PASS at v2.4.126, so this release introduces no
render regression.

recent_commits.message: fix: act on the final verification pass; package is now lint-clean
recent_commits.body:
An independent pass re-derived all eight behavioural claims in fresh
processes against a real paper (identical version dict before vs after
importing every engine; 245ms/16ms; byte-identical default render at
21776 chars vs standard 21777 and none 22487; 12/12 CLI sections carrying
subheadings; zero bare "pdftotext" literals). All eight held. It also found
what follows.

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_v2.4.126.md contained a FALSE claim: "both consumer
surfaces now derive from the dataclass" was true of the library CLI and
false of the service, which still hand-enumerated nine keys and still
dropped `subheadings`. Fixed the data loss rather than only the sentence —
`Section.subheadings` has existed since sectioning v1.6.1, so the service
can emit it against the CURRENT 2.4.125 pin; the switch to Section.to_dict()
stays queued for after the bump. API.md's schema gains the key, and its
`pages` row no longer implies PDF populates it (nothing does).

Three code defects, each reproduced first:
- batch.py imported `fields` and never used it.
- sections/__init__.py annotated `normalization_level` with a forward ref to
  a name imported only inside the function body, so
  typing.get_type_hints(extract_sections) raised NameError. Module-level
  import; verified no cycle (normalize's back-import is lazy, and importing
  docpluck.sections first in a fresh process resolves).
- an unused import in the test module.

Then the lint the sweep implied, all pre-existing: three unused locals
INSPECTED rather than deleted (an assigned-but-unused value in extraction
logic is the "silently dropped computed value" class — all three were
vestigial, none was a lost value), one dead local in SectionedDocument.all()
removed after verifying every documented case still resolves, and four
unused imports. `ruff --select F401,F811,F841` now passes clean over
docpluck/.

Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed, md5-verified against the tested tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: fix(provenance): four surfaces claimed what the call graph did not do
recent_commits.body:
Second, max-effort pass over the v2.4.126 work. The first pass fixed the
reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and
three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in
the code. Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed (2015 baseline + 46 new).

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also
reports pdftotext_path (the exact binary, resolved once and used by the
extraction call sites too, so the receipt cannot name a build that did not
run), pdfminer.six, pypdfium2, opencv, mammoth, beautifulsoup4, lxml --
two of three input formats were unpinned entirely -- plus python_version
and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

recent_commits.message: feat(provenance): report every input that can change output (v2.4.126)
recent_commits.body:
MetaESCI asks A-1/A-2. A docpluck SHA did not pin extraction: the same SHA
(a5c02ef) against the same PDF (10.1098/rsos.202336) produced 49,091 vs
50,101 normalized chars across a poppler binary replacement, and
get_version_info() reported three keys that were identical in both runs.

Fixes the class, not the symptom. get_version_info() now reports the
pdftotext binary version AND engine (poppler/xpdf differ behaviourally and
share a banner), poppler_version, pdfplumber, camelot, plus the in-repo
sectioning_version and table_extraction_version that were exported and
bumped independently of the package version but never on the receipt.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION is now exported from the package top level.

ExtractionReport carries the same; ExtractionFileResult gains
n_replacement_chars and n_greek_chars (A-2), measured on the normalized
output.

Sibling defects found by sweeping for the same shape:
- NormalizationReport.to_dict() was silently dropping
  column_interleave_pages, a populated field extract_columns documents as
  the canonical source of that signal. Live, predates this change.
- The per-file sidecar recorded ok:false on every SUCCESSFUL extraction,
  and an elapsed_seconds:0.0 written before the timer stopped.
All three hand-enumerated serializers now derive from asdict().

Also: INBOX_* was missing from .gitignore's cross-project correspondence
block, so an inbox doc had been committed to this public repo (unpushed;
those commits were dropped). Duplicate L-010 heading renumbered.

31 tests, all verified failing against the unfixed code first. Full suite
2046 passed / 0 failed.

recent_commits.message: Remove cap_gate_size() and cap_gate_unknown(): dead code with misleading docs
recent_commits.body:
Neither function is called anywhere in R/, inst/ or vignettes/ -- the only
references were their own definitions, their manual pages, and tests written
directly against them.

Their documentation also describes behaviour the package does not have. Both
say a repository that exceeds a size limit is refused whole rather than
partially downloaded. download_repo_files() does the opposite: max_file_size
is a per-file filter that skips oversize files individually while the rest of
the repository still downloads, and max_download_size is a budget that keeps
already-cached files for free, then adds the smallest still-missing files
until the next one would exceed it, reporting what was omitted. Leaving these
functions in place invites someone to reintroduce all-or-nothing refusal on
the strength of a docstring.

cap_gate_count() stays, because a count cap genuinely should skip the whole
unit: half a codebook's LLM chunks describe half its variables. Its
description no longer refers to cap_gate_size() and now states why counts and
sizes are treated differently.

The five tests in test-cap-report.R that exercised the two removed functions
are deleted with them; the cap_gate_count() test remains.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: github_tree_files(): list every repository, like all other archive sources
recent_commits.body:
GitHub was the only archive source with a listing gate: a repository over
500 MB or over 1000 files returned files = NULL and contributed nothing --
not a truncated list, an absent one. OSF, Zenodo, ResearchBox, PsychArchives
and local directories have always been listed in full at any size.

The gate made sense when listing meant github_files(recursive = TRUE), an
N-request crawl of /contents/ where a large repository really did cost
hundreds of API calls. github_tree_files() fetches the whole tree from the
Git Trees API in one request regardless of size, so listing a 900 MB
repository costs exactly what listing a 2 MB one costs. Backwards, too:
gate = FALSE fell back to the expensive recursive crawl the gate was
supposedly protecting against.

Size still matters for downloading, and that is handled where it belongs.
download_repo_files() applies a per-file cap and a per-repository budget,
filling smallest-file-first and reporting what it omitted.

The caller in inst/modules/repo_check.R already passes no gate arguments and
carries a comment saying a repository is listed in full whatever its size, so
until now the code and its comment disagreed and large repositories were
silently dropped from listings.

Removed: the max_repo_size_mb, max_files and gate parameters, both gate
checks, and the dead github_files(recursive = TRUE) fallback. The signature
becomes github_tree_files(repo).

Kept: the tree$truncated guard for GitHub's own hard API limit above about
100,000 entries, where the response is genuinely incomplete. It still returns
files = NULL with a clear reason rather than a partial list.

recent_commits.message: Detect negative p-values and stop collapsing duplicate findings
recent_commits.body:
Adds a check for impossible negative p-values (issue #351) and fixes a
counting bug that hid genuine findings from the imprecise and zero
p-value tables.

Negative p-values are found with their own pattern, because
extract_p_values() cannot match a leading minus sign, so such values are
currently dropped entirely rather than reported. They are kept out of the
p-value table, counted as n_negative, and reported in their own section
only when at least one is found. A hit sets the traffic light to red.

Separately, report_table and zero_table were passed through unique() on
the matched text and its sentence. When one sentence contained two
distinct problems written identically, the second was discarded. Removing
unique() makes the report tables agree with the summary table counts.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real

recent_commits.message: Remove cap_gate_size() and cap_gate_unknown(): dead code with misleading docs
recent_commits.body:
Neither function is called anywhere in R/, inst/ or vignettes/ -- the only
references were their own definitions, their manual pages, and tests written
directly against them.

Their documentation also describes behaviour the package does not have. Both
say a repository that exceeds a size limit is refused whole rather than
partially downloaded. download_repo_files() does the opposite: max_file_size
is a per-file filter that skips oversize files individually while the rest of
the repository still downloads, and max_download_size is a budget that keeps
already-cached files for free, then adds the smallest still-missing files
until the next one would exceed it, reporting what was omitted. Leaving these
functions in place invites someone to reintroduce all-or-nothing refusal on
the strength of a docstring.

cap_gate_count() stays, because a count cap genuinely should skip the whole
unit: half a codebook's LLM chunks describe half its variables. Its
description no longer refers to cap_gate_size() and now states why counts and
sizes are treated differently.

The five tests in test-cap-report.R that exercised the two removed functions
are deleted with them; the cap_gate_count() test remains.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: github_tree_files(): list every repository, like all other archive sources
recent_commits.body:
GitHub was the only archive source with a listing gate: a repository over
500 MB or over 1000 files returned files = NULL and contributed nothing --
not a truncated list, an absent one. OSF, Zenodo, ResearchBox, PsychArchives
and local directories have always been listed in full at any size.

The gate made sense when listing meant github_files(recursive = TRUE), an
N-request crawl of /contents/ where a large repository really did cost
hundreds of API calls. github_tree_files() fetches the whole tree from the
Git Trees API in one request regardless of size, so listing a 900 MB
repository costs exactly what listing a 2 MB one costs. Backwards, too:
gate = FALSE fell back to the expensive recursive crawl the gate was
supposedly protecting against.

Size still matters for downloading, and that is handled where it belongs.
download_repo_files() applies a per-file cap and a per-repository budget,
filling smallest-file-first and reporting what it omitted.

The caller in inst/modules/repo_check.R already passes no gate arguments and
carries a comment saying a repository is listed in full whatever its size, so
until now the code and its comment disagreed and large repositories were
silently dropped from listings.

Removed: the max_repo_size_mb, max_files and gate parameters, both gate
checks, and the dead github_files(recursive = TRUE) fallback. The signature
becomes github_tree_files(repo).

Kept: the tree$truncated guard for GitHub's own hard API limit above about
100,000 entries, where the response is genuinely incomplete. It still returns
files = NULL with a clear reason rather than a partial list.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Detect negative p-values and stop collapsing duplicate findings
recent_commits.body:
Adds a check for impossible negative p-values (issue #351) and fixes a
counting bug that hid genuine findings from the imprecise and zero
p-value tables.

Negative p-values are found with their own pattern, because
extract_p_values() cannot match a leading minus sign, so such values are
currently dropped entirely rather than reported. They are kept out of the
p-value table, counted as n_negative, and reported in their own section
only when at least one is found. A hit sets the traffic light to red.

Separately, report_table and zero_table were passed through unique() on
the matched text and its sentence. When one sentence contained two
distinct problems written identically, the second was discarded. Removing
unique() makes the report tables agree with the summary table counts.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): snapshot suite resolved fixtures under the pre-2026-08-03 Vibe root
recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12
byte-for-byte extraction tests SKIPPED — silently, reporting green.

Before: 24 skipped in 0.17s.  After: 25 passed in 201.80s.

This is verbatim the failure the portfolio hard rule warns about ("a discovery
helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a
clean one" — the same rule notes the 2026-08-03 move went unnoticed for five
weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,
and a new test_fixture_root_exists FAILS when the root is absent. A missing
individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

recent_commits.message: Move the trial-level file screener in from the Behaverse converter
recent_commits.body:
.bh_is_trial_level_file() and .eprime_is_export() were defined in
R/behaverse-convert.R, which meant data_check depended on an 808-line format
CONVERTER to answer a CLASSIFICATION question -- and used exactly one function
out of it, never converting anything.

Deciding whether a file holds trial-level behavioural data (one row per trial)
rather than a participant-level table (one row per respondent) is the same kind
of question as data_check_is_behaverse/inquisit/jspsych/psychopy(), which these
two functions delegate to and which already live here. Moved so they sit with
the detectors they use.

data_check uses the verdict to keep trial-level task output out of its
tabular-data counts and column descriptions: a per-trial file's columns are
paradata channels (response times, trial indices, stimulus codes), so
describing them as variables of a participant-level dataset produces noise. The
verdict is recorded as `data_format = "trial_level"` in data_check's per-file
`structure` table.

That leaves the Behaverse converter free to be a separate, later step: it reads
data_check's structure table to find the files already marked trial-level,
rather than re-deciding, and nothing in the check pipeline depends on it.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: repo_check: list what is inside .zip archives instead of just counting them
recent_commits.body:
An archive was a dead end in the listing. repo_check reported "this repository
contains 3 archive files" and could say nothing about what a reader would
actually get — while already recommending .zip over .7z/.rar/.tar.gz precisely
BECAUSE only ZIP can be inspected without downloading. It knew about the
capability without using it.

A ZIP stores its central directory at the END of the file, so one HTTP Range
request for the tail recovers every entry's name and uncompressed size without
fetching the archive (zip_peek(), added in the previous commit). That is the
same "list, don't fetch" operation this module is built around, so it belongs
here rather than waiting for data_check to download.

When the peek succeeds the archive row is REPLACED by its contents, so the
listing shows the files rather than the container, and those files flow into
classification, naming checks and study grouping like any other. Each entry
gets:
  * file_path prefixed with the archive's own name, so a reader can see where
    a file came from and two archives holding a `data.csv` do not collide;
  * file_url = NA, since an entry inside an archive is not separately
    downloadable and nothing downstream should try;
  * file_type re-derived from the INNER extension. Left inherited it would
    still read "archive" for every entry, so a zip of 40 CSVs would report 40
    archives and zero data files (files_data/files_code/files_zip all key on
    this column).

Controlled by the new `peek_zips` argument, default TRUE. It costs one Range
request per .zip; set FALSE to leave archives opaque and make no per-archive
request.

A failed peek — a host that ignores Range requests, or a directory not in the
tail — leaves the archive row untouched, and data_check opens it after
download as before. Formats with no tail index (.7z/.rar/.tar.gz) are never
peekable, so the "prefer .zip" recommendation now reports exactly the archives
that stayed opaque.

Also fixes the classification call, which passed only file_name and so
discarded the folder signal: data_classify_files() keys its keyword tier on
the PATH too, which is how a generically-named file inside `Materials/` is
recognised. data_check has always passed both.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add zip-peek: read a remote archive's contents without downloading it
recent_commits.body:
R/zip-peek.R reads a ZIP's file listing over HTTP without fetching the
archive. A ZIP stores its central directory at the END of the file, so a
single HTTP Range request for the tail is enough to recover every entry's
name and uncompressed size. zip_decision() builds on that to answer "is this
archive worth downloading?" -- an archive holding only stimuli or media is
better linked than mirrored, and that can now be decided before spending the
bandwidth.

Added to this PR because listing what a repository contains is repo_check's
job, and an archive is currently a dead end in that listing: repo_check
reports "this repository contains 3 archive files" and can say nothing about
what is inside them. It already flags a NON-.zip archive precisely because
only ZIP can be inspected this way -- it knows about the capability without
being able to use it. Wiring the peek into repo_check's own listing is a
follow-up; this commit adds the machinery it needs.

Falls back to NULL when a host does not honour range requests or the central
directory is not in the tail, so a caller can download-and-inspect instead.
.expand_zip()/.expand_tar()/.expand_compressed() handle the download-and-open
path for archives that cannot be peeked, or that are already local.

Depends on #346 for .data_doc_role() and .data_group_from_path(), which this
PR already requires for check_file_naming().
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: repo_check: drop the GitHub listing gate parameters
recent_commits.body:
Follows the change to github_tree_files(), which now lists every repository
in full whatever its size, matching how OSF, Zenodo, ResearchBox,
PsychArchives and local directories have always been treated. There is no
longer a gate to configure, so github_gate, github_max_repo_size_mb and
github_max_files are removed from repo_check()'s signature.

The warning for a repository that could not be listed no longer tells the
user to "Set `github_gate = FALSE`" -- that parameter is gone, and neither
remaining reason is one a parameter can fix: a repository is either invalid/
inaccessible, or its tree exceeds GitHub's own 100,000-item API limit and
comes back truncated.

How much of a repository is DOWNLOADED is unchanged and still capped, by
download_repo_files()'s per-file and per-repository budgets in data_check.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: github_tree_files(): list every repository, like all other archive sources
recent_commits.body:
GitHub was the only archive source with a listing gate: a repository over
500 MB or 1000 files returned files = NULL and contributed nothing at all --
not a truncated list, an absent one. OSF, Zenodo, ResearchBox, PsychArchives
and local directories have always been listed in full at any size.

That gate made sense when listing meant github_files(recursive = TRUE), an
N-request crawl of /contents/ where a large repository really did cost
hundreds of API calls. It no longer does. github_tree_files() fetches the
entire tree from the Git Trees API in ONE request regardless of size, so
listing a 900 MB repository costs exactly what listing a 2 MB one costs.
The gate was refusing repositories that are cheap to list -- and, backwards,
`gate = FALSE` fell back to the EXPENSIVE recursive crawl it was supposedly
protecting against.

Size does still matter for DOWNLOADING, and that is already handled where it
belongs: download_repo_files() applies a per-file cap and a per-repository
budget, filling smallest-file-first up to max_download_size and reporting
what it omitted.

Removed: the max_repo_size_mb and max_files parameters, both gate checks, and
the `gate` argument (with its dead github_files(recursive = TRUE) fallback).

Kept: the tree$truncated guard. That is GitHub's own hard API limit -- above
about 100,000 entries the response is incomplete, and there is no way to list
such a repository through this endpoint. It still returns files = NULL with a
clear reason rather than silently yielding a partial file list.

github_tree_files() is now github_tree_files(repo).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Remove cap_gate_size() and cap_gate_unknown(): dead code with misleading docs
recent_commits.body:
Both were defined and exported but never called anywhere in the package.
cap_gate_size() appeared only in a cross-reference inside cap_gate_count()'s
own documentation; cap_gate_unknown() had no references at all.

Worse, cap_gate_size()'s documentation actively misdescribed the package's
behaviour. It stated that size caps are "an upfront, all-or-nothing gate:
when a repository cannot be downloaded in full within the size limits, the
whole repository is refused rather than partially downloaded". That is not
what happens. download_repo_files() sorts the missing files smallest-first
and takes them until max_download_size is spent, then reports what it left
out ("downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, N files omitted. Raise
`max_download_size` to include more."). A reader trusting the docstring would
have the download policy exactly backwards.

cap_gate_count() is kept -- codebook_check() calls it twice -- and its
roxygen no longer references the deleted function. It now also states the
distinction the removed docs got wrong: a COUNT cap skips the whole unit
because half a codebook's LLM chunks describe half its variables, whereas a
SIZE limit fills to the budget and reports the remainder.

Removed from this PR before it merges so neither becomes exported API:
  - cap_gate_size(), cap_gate_unknown() (R/report-helpers.R)
  - their exports from NAMESPACE
  - man/cap_gate_size.Rd, man/cap_gate_unknown.Rd
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Remove data_analysis_unit(): inferred a unit of observation nothing consumed
recent_commits.body:
data_analysis_unit() guessed what one row of a data file represents (person /
trial / session / dyad) from column-name patterns and identifier uniqueness,
and data_check rendered a per-file table plus a warning when a repository
mixed units.

Nothing ever acted on the result. The value was written into data_check's
column table and printed in its report, and that was the end of it: it is not
written to the manifest, and despite the documentation citing DDI
`analysisUnit` it never reaches the Psych-DS or DDI export. No other module
reads it.

The inference was also weakest exactly where it mattered most. With one
identifier column that repeats and no trial/session column present, it falls
through to guessing "trial", which is wrong for any long-format survey that
does not happen to name a column "wave" or "session". And the 0.98 uniqueness
threshold means a person-level file with a few duplicate participant ids -- a
real data-quality problem worth surfacing -- is silently relabelled
"trial" instead of flagged.

Removed here, before this PR merges, so it never becomes exported API:
  - data_analysis_unit() and .analysis_unit_patterns (R/data_check_helpers.R)
  - export(data_analysis_unit) from NAMESPACE
  - man/data_analysis_unit.Rd
  - its test block in tests/testthat/test-data-checks.R

The data_check call sites and the "Unit of Observation" report section are
removed separately, in the data_check module's own change.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: code_check: read code from output files, add Python/notebook support, and detect environment pins
recent_commits.body:
Depends on:
  - the stat_helpers PR (this branch is based on it) for .spv_export_syntax(),
    .smcl_export_syntax(), .mplus_export_syntax(), .html_export_r_source()
    and .html_sniff_kind()
  - #341 (repo-download) for download_repo_files()
  - #346 (data_check_helpers) for manifest_merge()

BREAKING: the file_limit argument is REMOVED. Previously only the first 20
files per repository were analysed, which silently skipped code in any
repository larger than that. Coverage is now bounded by SIZE rather than
file count: max_file_size (default 100 MB per file) and max_download_size
(default 500 MB per repository), both settable to Inf. Every code file within
those caps is checked.

READS CODE FROM OUTPUT FILES. Analysis syntax is frequently shared only as
rendered output, with no separate script. Four new expanders recover it and
add it to the file list as a real sibling code file, so it is then checked
like any other script:
  .spv   (SPSS output)   -> .sps, from the structure XML that records the
                            syntax which produced each result
  .smcl  (Stata log)     -> .do,  from the commands echoed verbatim in the log
  .out   (Mplus output)  -> .inp, from its own INPUT INSTRUCTIONS section
  .html  (rendered Rmd/  -> .R,   after content-sniffing to tell analysis
          Quarto)                 output from a task-runner or docs page
Each is gated on a file-extension check, so a repository without those file
types does no extra work. .code_predownload() fetches what the expanders need.

PYTHON AND NOTEBOOKS. code_extract_py() and code_extract_qmd_py() extract
Python the way code_extract_r() extracts R. code_lang() no longer trusts the
extension for .ipynb or .qmd: both are polyglot, so the declared kernel is
read from inside the file (.ipynb_lang(), .qmd_lang()). Checked against a real
corpus of 144 cached notebooks -- 126 declared Python, 7 declared R, every one
of them via metadata inside the file. Two of those R notebooks opened with
library(rethinking); treating them as Python found zero packages in a file
that plainly loads five. Python remains the fallback when the file cannot be
read yet (a URL, not downloaded), since it is by far the more common kernel.

ENVIRONMENT PINS. .code_version_pin_check() detects renv.lock (plus the R
version and locked packages it records), groundhog.library() and checkpoint()
date-pins, and a sessionInfo.txt dump by both filename and content. It
requires an actual pin, not merely a library(groundhog) call. A repository
with no pinned environment is now flagged as a reproducibility gap.

PACKAGE INVENTORY AND MANIFEST. code_packages() and code_library_names()
record the packages loaded per file and per paper. The new manifest argument
merges the distinct packages into a manifest's `code` section via
manifest_merge(), preserving any files/provenance written by data_check.

CACHING. The new cache argument (default FALSE) keeps downloaded code in the
persistent on-disk cache (repo_cache_dir()) for reuse on later runs; FALSE
downloads to a temporary directory discarded when the session ends.

CHANGES TO EXISTING FUNCTIONS. code_abs_path(), code_file_refs(), code_lang(),
code_library_lines(), code_line_stats() and code_remove_comments() all gain
Python support, plus two bug fixes: comment stripping mis-counted lines that
hold both code and a trailing comment, and comment markers inside string
literals were treated as comments in Stata and MATLAB (both issue #261).
code_file_refs() also now detects rio::import()/import_list() file references.

Tests: 25 new blocks across test-code_check.R and test-module-code_check.R,
including a regression test that downloaded files keep their analysis results
through the join, and one confirming all code files are checked now that the
per-repository cap is gone.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add statistics output pipeline with a shared stat_helpers.R
recent_commits.body:
Adds the readers that recover statistical results from analysis OUTPUT files,
plus a new R/stat_helpers.R holding the small, format-agnostic utilities they
share.

WHY stat_helpers.R exists

These helpers were each defined in whichever file happened to need one first,
then called from several others. That made the cluster impossible to split:
code_check's syntax recovery needed two one-line formatters and therefore had
to pull in the whole of R/r-output.R and R/stat-tables.R. Collecting them in
one file means a caller can reuse a formatter without sourcing an unrelated
format reader, and a helper shared by the paper-prose path and the output path
(notably .r_stat_pattern(), which extract_eq() and read_r_output() must agree
on) has a single home so the two cannot drift apart.

Thirteen helpers moved, unchanged except where noted:
  numbers/text   .stat_num_to_chr, .stat_display_value, .stat_html_escape
  identifiers    .stat_sanitize_id
  statistic names .norm_stat_name, .stato_strip_variant
  reported values .norm_value, .norm_interval
  table cells    .STAT_PLACEHOLDERS, .stat_is_placeholder,
                 .stat_is_label_col, .table_header_ambiguous
  shared pattern .r_stat_pattern

Two are renamed, because their old names claimed a format specificity they
never had:
  .spv_html_escape()   -> .stat_html_escape()
  .spv_display_value() -> .stat_display_value()
Neither has anything SPSS-specific in it. .spv_html_escape() in particular had
five callers, four of which (the Stata and Mplus HTML exporters, and the
data_check and data_validate report tables) have nothing to do with .spv files
at all. All call sites are updated.

Nothing in stat_helpers.R knows about a specific file format; format-specific
parsing stays in its own file.

WHAT ELSE IS HERE

  R/spv.R          SPSS .spv reader (light-binary and legacy table formats),
                   HTML export, chart rendering, and syntax recovery
  R/stata.R        Stata .smcl log reader, HTML export, syntax recovery
  R/mplus.R        Mplus .out reader, HTML export, syntax recovery
  R/html-output.R  sniffing rendered RMarkdown/Quarto HTML and recovering its
                   R source
  R/jasp.R         JASP .jasp reader (its embedded SQLite) and HTML export
  R/omv.R          jamovi .omv reader (protobuf) and HTML export
  R/stat-tables.R  read_stat_tables(): JASP/jamovi/ipynb result tables
  R/r-output.R     read_r_output(): results from captured R console output
  R/r-capture.R    capturing results from a running R session
  R/stat-output.R  serialising extracted tables to a flat data.frame and to a
                   metacheck-native JSON statistical-output document
  R/stato-map.R    column header -> STATO ontology typing
  R/extract-tests.R grouping extracted components into whole tests
  R/match-reported.R / R/match-table.R  matching results reported in the paper
                   against results found in the outputs

New dependencies: DBI and RSQLite (Suggests) to read JASP's embedded SQLite;
graphics and grDevices (Imports) to render .spv charts with base R only.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
