stat_p_exact additionally distinguishes a table's footnote text (which the

recent_commits.message: Add Zenodo bulk-archive download, ResearchBox re-scrape fix, PsychArchives support, and GitHub tree API
recent_commits.body:
Depends on the archive-osf PR (#341) for .repo_cache_subdir(), used by
rbox_file_download() below. Please merge #341 first, or merge together.

R/archive-zenodo.R:
- zenodo_links() adds the same bare-DOI body-text fallback osf_links() and
  rbox_links() already use (e.g. "10.5281/zenodo.1234567" cited with no
  URL scheme at all), plus trailing-slash normalisation so a real hyperlink
  and a bare mention of the same record are not double-counted.
- zenodo_file_download() now tries Zenodo's files-archive endpoint first --
  a single request for the whole record as one zip, used only when every
  file in the record survived the earlier size filters (so the archive's
  contents are exactly the files wanted, no wasted transport). Falls back
  to the previous file-by-file download for any file the bulk archive did
  not account for.

R/archive-researchbox.R:
- ResearchBox sits behind Cloudflare, which returns HTTP 406 for httr2's
  default User-Agent; added .rbox_headers() (browser-like Accept/User-Agent)
  to every request, the same workaround archive-aspredicted.R already uses.
- rbox_links() adds the same bare-mention body-text fallback (e.g.
  "researchbox.org/801" with no real hyperlink).
- rbox_file_download() is a real bug fix: ResearchBox no longer serves a
  static zip URL (the previous s3.wasabisys.com guess now 404s -- issue
  #186). The site instead generates the zip on request from a POST to
  download_files.php, given a box_id, reference token, and file ids scraped
  off the box's own page -- .rbox_info() now scrapes and returns these.
  Downloads are also cached persistently (keyed by the ResearchBox URL,
  via .repo_cache_subdir() from #341) instead of a temp dir, so a re-run
  reuses the already-downloaded/unzipped files.

R/archive-psycharchives.R (new): PsychArchives link detection, info
retrieval, and file download -- same three-function shape as the other
archive sources (*_links/*_info/*_file_download).

R/archive-github.R: adds github_tree_files(), which fetches a repository's
complete file tree via the Git Trees API in two requests (repo metadata +
recursive tree) instead of the N-request recursive /contents/ crawl
github_files() uses, and gates large or software-dominated repositories
(by disk size or file count) before any recursive traversal is attempted.

R/archive-local.R: local_files() no longer errors on a path that does not
yet exist (mustWork = FALSE on normalizePath()).

recent_commits.message: Add shared repo-download cache and size/count cap-gate infrastructure
recent_commits.body:
archive-osf.R (this branch) uses .download_many_parallel() from a new
R/repo-download.R, which did not exist on dev. This commit adds the full
dependency chain so the branch is self-contained:

- R/repo-download.R (new): download_repo_files() plus a persistent,
  rappdirs-style on-disk cache (repo_cache_dir(), repo_cache_size(),
  repo_cache_clear()) keyed per repository, so re-running a check does not
  re-download files already fetched. Parallel downloads via
  req_perform_parallel() in production, falling back to sequential requests
  under testthat (httptest2 does not mock parallel requests).
- R/cache.R (new): metacheck_cache_info(), a single entry point reporting on
  both on-disk caches (the repo cache here and the LLM response cache from
  R/llm-cache.R, see the llm PR).
- R/cap-prompt.R (new): cap_report(), the shared way a resource cap reports
  what was skipped -- printed immediately (so a looped run shows each
  refusal against the right item, not batched at the end) and raised as a
  warning for programmatic capture via warnings()/tryCatch.
- R/report-helpers.R: adds cap_gate_size(), cap_gate_count(), and
  cap_gate_unknown(), which build the actual cap-refusal messages
  cap_report() prints -- a size gate (per-file and per-repository download
  limits), a count gate (e.g. codebook_max_calls), and the fallback for a
  file whose size could not be determined at all. All three follow the same
  policy: caps are all-or-nothing (a unit of work that cannot fit within the
  limits is skipped in full, never partially done), and every message names
  the parameter and the value needed to lift the cap on a future run.

Note: this PR depends on the LLM response-cache PR (adds R/llm-cache.R),
since metacheck_cache_info() calls .llm_cache_dir(). Please merge that PR
first, or merge both together.

metacheck_cache_info() does not yet have test coverage; flagging rather than
adding tests outside this PR's stated scope.

recent_commits.message: Add OSF listing cache, pagination/parallel fetching, zip download mode, and reliability fixes
recent_commits.body:
Reliability fixes:
- osf_links() now also catches bare body-text mentions like "osf.io/gms8z/"
  that the source PDF/HTML never encoded as a real hyperlink, in addition to
  the paper's own url table -- same two-tier approach github_links() already
  uses. Trailing slashes are normalised so a hyperlink and a bare mention of
  the same project don't get double-counted as two different repos.
- osf_get_all_pages() distinguishes a genuinely empty listing from a request
  that could not be completed (private/embargoed/withdrawn/deleted resource,
  or a network failure). Failures are returned as an empty list() carrying an
  osf_error attribute ("forbidden"/"not_found"/"gone"/"request_failed"),
  since a bare NULL cannot carry attributes in R. Existing callers that only
  check length(result) == 0 are unaffected.
- osf_type() returns "inaccessible" (distinct from NA) when the GUID is
  validly formed but the resource itself could not be reached.
- osf_check_id() no longer errors on NA input or a bare link to osf.io itself
  (common as a generic citation), returning NA_character_ for both.

Performance:
- Ask OSF for page[size]=100 instead of the default 10 (.osf_max_page_size()),
  cutting sequential API calls for a large listing by ~10x.
- Once the total page count is known, remaining pages are computed up front
  and fetched in parallel via req_perform_parallel() instead of recursing
  one page at a time waiting on each response's `next` link. Requires
  httr2 >= 1.1.0 for req_perform_parallel(on_error = "continue")
  (DESCRIPTION updated accordingly). Falls back to the previous sequential
  behaviour under testthat, since httptest2 does not mock parallel requests.
- osf_info() listings are now cached for the session, keyed by (url,
  recursive), so a second pass over the same repository (e.g. report() then
  convert_psychds()) does not re-query OSF. Cleared via the new
  osf_cache_clear(), disabled via options(metacheck.osf.cache = FALSE).

New capability:
- osf_file_download() gains mode = c("files", "zip"): "zip" requests OSF's
  Waterbutler-generated zip of a whole folder/repository in one request
  instead of downloading files individually, with an unzip = TRUE/FALSE
  option for what to do with the archive afterwards. Streams to disk with
  progress messages, since Waterbutler generates the archive server-side
  first, which can take minutes for a large repository before any bytes
  arrive.

tests/testthat/helper.R gains a redactor that strips the new page[size]=100
query parameter before matching against recorded mocks, so existing OSF
fixtures remain valid without needing to be re-captured.

recent_commits.message: Add LLM response cache, reasoning-effort/max-tokens controls, and reliability fixes
recent_commits.body:
Reliability fixes to llm():
- Sanitise text for invalid UTF-8 and control characters before caching or
  sending, since research free-text routinely breaks JSON serialisation
  (observed as Mistral HTTP 400 "error parsing the body")
- Surface the provider's actual error detail instead of a bare HTTP status
  (.llm_error_message())
- Retry structured-output calls up to 5x on transient schema/JSON failures
  from Groq, which are not deterministic server-side (.llm_json_retryable())
- Detect systemic failures (auth, 5xx, unreachable endpoint) and emit one
  immediate message() per session, since queued warning()s are invisible
  mid-run and checks would otherwise silently fall back to rules-only
- Fix empty-result edge cases: a 0-row structured response no longer errors
  on join-key assignment; an all-empty response set no longer breaks the
  final left_join
- Reword the summary warning to state how many rows succeeded vs failed

New capabilities:
- On-disk response cache (R/llm-cache.R): llm() runs at temperature 0, so
  identical (model, prompt, text, type, params) calls are deterministic and
  can be replayed from disk instead of re-billing the provider. Controlled
  via llm_cache()/llm_cache_clear()
- llm_max_tokens(): session-wide default so callers do not need to repeat
  params = list(max_tokens = ...) in every module
- llm_reasoning(): session-wide reasoning-effort default, translated per
  model family (gpt-oss, qwen3, Mistral, Ollama each use a different
  mechanism/value set, verified against each provider's actual behaviour).
  Defaults to "low" since every call this package makes is bounded
  extraction/classification, not multi-step reasoning
- vllm/<model> routing via chat_vllm() for custom vLLM endpoints
- phase argument labels the progress bar with the calling step instead of a
  generic "Extracting data"
- llm_model(NULL) now actually clears the model (previously there was no way
  to unset it, since is.null(model) meant "read")

llm() now validates model and params up front, before any network work.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

recent_commits.body:
`test_v2_backwards_compat.py` hardcoded `$HOME/Dropbox/Vibe`. The portfolio
moved OUT of Dropbox on 2026-08-03 (Dropbox syncing a live .git corrupts
repos), so every fixture resolved to a path that no longer exists and all 12

helper that returns empty when the root is wrong makes a broken run look like a

weeks while weekly reviews 'passed'). Now resolves VIBE_ROOT then $HOME/Vibe,

individual PDF stays a legitimate skip (not everyone has the closed-access
corpus); a missing ROOT is a broken configuration and must be visible.

All 12 snapshots still match byte-for-byte, so extract_pdf() output has not
drifted since 2026-05-07 — including across the 2026-05-14 poppler swap, on
these papers.

NOT FIXED HERE, needs a user decision: those 12 snapshots are 984 KB of
published article text, git-tracked and live on the PUBLIC remote since
7b04f8f. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, which a sha256 gives
identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

linking only Zenodo/ResearchBox/PsychArchives), not an edge case. Falls back
to the paper's own id.

New: PsychArchives repositories are listed via its DSpace REST API. Files are
matched on file_url AND file_path rather than file_name alone, since
file_name is not unique across folders.

New: GitHub repositories can be gated before any recursive listing
(github_gate, github_max_repo_size_mb, github_max_files), so an oversized or
software-dominated repo is refused up front rather than discovered part-way
through a crawl. Uses github_tree_files() from #342, which reads the whole
tree in two API requests.

New: R/file-naming.R adds check_file_naming(), a preliminary name- and
path-only review of a repository's file organisation. It is deliberately
name-only because repo_check never downloads files. Root readme and
ro-crate-metadata.json are treated as collection-level and never flagged.
Guards NA file_path values, which occur in a mixed multi-source file list
(e.g. OSF plus local) even when other rows have a path.

The module also gains optional model/params arguments, used only when
llm_use(TRUE), for the study-grouping pass.

recent_commits.message: power: use structured LLM extraction with prompt-based fallback
recent_commits.body:
The power module previously built its system prompt by fetching
https://scienceverse.org/schema/power.json at runtime and asking the model to
return JSON in a fenced block, then parsing that text. That depends on a live
network fetch of the schema on every run, and on the model formatting its
reply correctly.

It now uses ellmer's structured-output mode with a type spec built in R
(type_object()/type_array()), so the provider validates the shape rather than
metacheck parsing free text. The spec is written by hand rather than via
ellmer::type_from_schema() on the shipped schema, because that schema uses
null-inclusive enums, which some providers' structured-output validators
reject outright.

When a provider does not support structured output for this schema, the
module falls back to the previous prompt-based extraction and says so in its
report, rather than failing. Per-row LLM errors are tracked separately from a
wholesale failure, so a run where only some paragraphs failed still reports
the paragraphs that succeeded.

Depends on the data_check_helpers PR for .strip_llm_wrapper(), which strips
the wrapper-object prefix ellmer returns when a structured schema wraps its
array in a single object field (needed because some providers reject a bare
top-level array).

recent_commits.message: Add data_check_helpers: file classification, codebook parsing, and column-level data checks
recent_commits.body:
Adds R/data_check_helpers.R, the shared helper layer the data-checking modules
are built on. It is added ahead of those modules so it can be reviewed on its
own; nothing on dev calls it yet.

Three groups of functions:

FILE CLASSIFICATION
data_classify_files() assigns each repository file a semantic type (data,
codebook, code, materials, ...) from its name and extension; data_format()
maps an extension to a format label; data_is_manifest() recognises a
table-of-contents file that describes other files rather than holding data.
manifest_merge() merges a manifest patch into an existing one.

READING AND SNIFFING
data_read_head() reads the first rows of a tabular file without loading it,
across delimited text, Excel, SPSS/Stata/SAS and RData, with delimiter
sniffing and header detection (.sniff_delimiter, .detect_header,
.detect_header_row). data_promote_header_row() fixes files whose real header
sits below junk rows; data_strip_qualtrics_header() removes Qualtrics' two
extra description rows. text_peek() and txt_classify_content() read and
classify a text file's content when the extension alone is not decisive.

COLUMN-LEVEL CHECKS AND CODEBOOKS
data_col_type(), data_col_stats(), data_col_concept() and data_col_facets()
describe a column; the data_check_* family flags specific problems (constant
or empty columns, outliers, whitespace, case inconsistency, numbers stored as
text, scale values outside their range, SPSS filter columns, colliding or
overlong column names, and several classes of potentially identifying
information). data_check_is_qualtrics/behaverse/inquisit/jspsych/psychopy
recognise data exported by common survey and experiment platforms.
parse_codebook() and parse_qsf() extract variable documentation from
codebooks in many formats (delimited, Excel, JSON, Markdown, PDF, rich text,
haven value labels, and Qualtrics .qsf survey definitions);
match_column_labels() aligns those variables with a dataset's actual columns.

data_group_llm() and data_study_roster() group a repository's files into
studies, using the paper's own text plus an LLM pass.

Tests: test-data-checks.R, test-data-read.R, test-data-manifest.R and
test-codebook-helpers.R. Note that 4 of the 39 test blocks in
test-data-checks.R call module_run(paper, "data_check"), which needs the
data_check MODULE (inst/modules/data_check.R) -- not part of this PR. Those
four will fail until the module lands; the other 35 exercise the helpers
directly and pass on their own.

recent_commits.message: Improve file classification, Grobid table extraction, and text/read helpers
recent_commits.body:
R/file_category.R: a statistics-package file that bundles BOTH a dataset and
its analyses (a .jasp / .por, typed "data;stats") is now classified as DATA,
since the dataset is the primary artifact and any bundled analyses are
recovered separately as the code file. Other compound types (code;web,
code;exec, code;data) keep their previous behaviour.

R/import-grobid.R: adds .tei_table_contents(), which reads a Grobid <table>
node's <row>/<cell> structure into a data frame. Grobid makes no header/data
distinction (unlike HTML's <th>/<td>), and a real table's header can span
several leading rows -- a super-header naming a group of columns, then a
sub-header, then the actual column names. A cell that spans several columns
carries a `cols` attribute (Grobid's equivalent of colspan); its text is
expanded across the columns it covers, using the same grid-alignment approach
.stat_table_parse() uses for JASP/jamovi colspans, so a spanning header cell
still lines up with the data columns beneath it rather than shifting
everything after it.

R/import-read.R and R/text-extractors.R: supporting extraction helpers.

Codebook filename detection now requires a TWO-WORD compound throughout, with
`[ _.-]?` separators so "code book", "code_book", "code-book" and dotted
export names like "Race_IAT.public.2025.codebook.csv" all match. The
two-word requirement is deliberate and was checked against 27k real
repository filenames: the single generic words are all substrings of ordinary
data files (meta_data.csv and encoding.csv in that corpus are participant and
trial-level DATA), so matching bare "metadata"/"codes"/"key" would steal real
datasets away from data_check -- worse than missing a codebook.

recent_commits.message: Rewrite ref_accuracy to check DOI-backed reference coherence; fix ref_consistency xref type
recent_commits.body:
ref_accuracy is substantially rewritten. It now checks whether each reference
that supplies its own DOI is internally COHERENT: the cited title, authors,
journal, year and DOI are compared field by field against the authoritative
record that the reference's DOI points to.

The key change is what is NOT checked. A reference with no DOI is no longer
compared against anything, because the only record available for it comes
from a CrossRef title search, which often returns the wrong paper -- any
resulting "mismatch" would be CrossRef's error rather than the citation's.
Such references are listed separately with a recommendation to add a DOI,
and a suggested DOI only when CrossRef found a high-confidence match
(suggest_score).

Comparison is deliberately tolerant of the ways PDF extraction goes wrong:

- Journal names match across standard ISO-4 abbreviations, "&"/"and", "the".
- Titles are compared by character-level similarity (title_similarity) after
  stripping case, punctuation, footnote markers and diacritics, so colons,
  em-dash spacing and line-break word splits do not flag.
- Only the leading max_authors surnames must match, since author lists are
  routinely truncated with "et al." and GROBID often drops the tail.
  Diacritics are ignored ("Gredeback" matches "Gredebäck").
- Year allows year_tolerance years of difference, since online-first and
  print years routinely differ by one.

DOI, journal and year flag a reference on their own. Title and author are
parsing-sensitive, so min_mismatches (default 1) controls how many of those
two must disagree.

Also fixes a documentation contradiction: the prose and validation text
described min_mismatches = 2 as the default while the signature defaults to
1. The prose now matches the code, and the validation block reports the same
numbers with the correct setting labelled as the default (~8% at the default
1, ~3% at the conservative 2).

ref_consistency: fixes the xref filter, which looked for xref_type "bib" but
the paper schema uses "bibr" -- so the module was silently matching nothing.

Supporting changes this depends on:

- R/db-crossref.R: crossref_doi() and crossref_query() now declare explicit
  throttles matching CrossRef's published polite-pool limits, effective
  2025-12-01 -- 10 req/s for single-record works/{doi} lookups, but only
  3 req/s for the list/search (query.*) endpoint. add_bib_match() now warns
  when lookups failed for NETWORK reasons (offline, timeout, 5xx) rather
  than because a DOI genuinely was not found, since a network failure leaves
  bib_match incomplete and downstream checks could misfire on it. Also fixes
  a copy-paste progress message in openalex_doi() ("Querying CrossRef by
  DOI" -> "Querying OpenAlex by DOI").
- R/utils.R: .batch_query() gains throttle_capacity/throttle_fill_time_s
  (NULL = no throttling, so unaffected callers are unchanged), plus internal
  path-length helpers for safe writes on Windows.

Depends on the archive-osf PR (#341) for .repo_cache_subdir(), used by
rbox_file_download() below. Please merge #341 first, or merge together.

R/archive-zenodo.R:
- zenodo_links() adds the same bare-DOI body-text fallback osf_links() and

  and a bare mention of the same record are not double-counted.

  a single request for the whole record as one zip, used only when every

  static zip URL (the previous s3.wasabisys.com guess now 404s -- issue
  #186). The site instead generates the zip on request from a POST to
  download_files.php, given a box_id, reference token, and file ids scraped
  off the box's own page -- .rbox_info() now scrapes and returns these.
  Downloads are also cached persistently (keyed by the ResearchBox URL,
  via .repo_cache_subdir() from #341) instead of a temp dir, so a re-run

retrieval, and file download -- same three-function shape as the other
archive sources (*_links/*_info/*_file_download).

R/archive-github.R: adds github_tree_files(), which fetches a repository's
complete file tree via the Git Trees API in two requests (repo metadata +
recursive tree) instead of the N-request recursive /contents/ crawl

(by disk size or file count) before any recursive traversal is attempted.

recent_commits.message: Add shared repo-download cache and size/count cap-gate infrastructure
recent_commits.body:
archive-osf.R (this branch) uses .download_many_parallel() from a new
R/repo-download.R, which did not exist on dev. This commit adds the full
dependency chain so the branch is self-contained:

- R/repo-download.R (new): download_repo_files() plus a persistent,
  rappdirs-style on-disk cache (repo_cache_dir(), repo_cache_size(),
  repo_cache_clear()) keyed per repository, so re-running a check does not
  re-download files already fetched. Parallel downloads via
  req_perform_parallel() in production, falling back to sequential requests
  under testthat (httptest2 does not mock parallel requests).
- R/cache.R (new): metacheck_cache_info(), a single entry point reporting on
  both on-disk caches (the repo cache here and the LLM response cache from
  R/llm-cache.R, see the llm PR).
- R/cap-prompt.R (new): cap_report(), the shared way a resource cap reports
  what was skipped -- printed immediately (so a looped run shows each
  refusal against the right item, not batched at the end) and raised as a
  warning for programmatic capture via warnings()/tryCatch.
- R/report-helpers.R: adds cap_gate_size(), cap_gate_count(), and
  cap_gate_unknown(), which build the actual cap-refusal messages
  cap_report() prints -- a size gate (per-file and per-repository download
  limits), a count gate (e.g. codebook_max_calls), and the fallback for a
  file whose size could not be determined at all. All three follow the same
  policy: caps are all-or-nothing (a unit of work that cannot fit within the
  limits is skipped in full, never partially done), and every message names
  the parameter and the value needed to lift the cap on a future run.

Note: this PR depends on the LLM response-cache PR (adds R/llm-cache.R),
since metacheck_cache_info() calls .llm_cache_dir(). Please merge that PR
first, or merge both together.

metacheck_cache_info() does not yet have test coverage; flagging rather than
adding tests outside this PR's stated scope.

recent_commits.message: Add OSF listing cache, pagination/parallel fetching, zip download mode, and reliability fixes
recent_commits.body:
Reliability fixes:
- osf_links() now also catches bare body-text mentions like "osf.io/gms8z/"
  that the source PDF/HTML never encoded as a real hyperlink, in addition to
  the paper's own url table -- same two-tier approach github_links() already
  uses. Trailing slashes are normalised so a hyperlink and a bare mention of
  the same project don't get double-counted as two different repos.
- osf_get_all_pages() distinguishes a genuinely empty listing from a request
  that could not be completed (private/embargoed/withdrawn/deleted resource,
  or a network failure). Failures are returned as an empty list() carrying an
  osf_error attribute ("forbidden"/"not_found"/"gone"/"request_failed"),
  since a bare NULL cannot carry attributes in R. Existing callers that only
  check length(result) == 0 are unaffected.
- osf_type() returns "inaccessible" (distinct from NA) when the GUID is
  validly formed but the resource itself could not be reached.
- osf_check_id() no longer errors on NA input or a bare link to osf.io itself
  (common as a generic citation), returning NA_character_ for both.

Performance:
- Ask OSF for page[size]=100 instead of the default 10 (.osf_max_page_size()),
  cutting sequential API calls for a large listing by ~10x.
- Once the total page count is known, remaining pages are computed up front
  and fetched in parallel via req_perform_parallel() instead of recursing
  one page at a time waiting on each response's `next` link. Requires
  httr2 >= 1.1.0 for req_perform_parallel(on_error = "continue")
  (DESCRIPTION updated accordingly). Falls back to the previous sequential
  behaviour under testthat, since httptest2 does not mock parallel requests.
- osf_info() listings are now cached for the session, keyed by (url,
  recursive), so a second pass over the same repository (e.g. report() then
  convert_psychds()) does not re-query OSF. Cleared via the new
  osf_cache_clear(), disabled via options(metacheck.osf.cache = FALSE).

New capability:
- osf_file_download() gains mode = c("files", "zip"): "zip" requests OSF's
  Waterbutler-generated zip of a whole folder/repository in one request
  instead of downloading files individually, with an unzip = TRUE/FALSE
  option for what to do with the archive afterwards. Streams to disk with
  progress messages, since Waterbutler generates the archive server-side
  first, which can take minutes for a large repository before any bytes
  arrive.

tests/testthat/helper.R gains a redactor that strips the new page[size]=100
query parameter before matching against recorded mocks, so existing OSF
fixtures remain valid without needing to be re-captured.

recent_commits.message: Add LLM response cache, reasoning-effort/max-tokens controls, and reliability fixes
recent_commits.body:
Reliability fixes to llm():
- Sanitise text for invalid UTF-8 and control characters before caching or
  sending, since research free-text routinely breaks JSON serialisation
  (observed as Mistral HTTP 400 "error parsing the body")
- Surface the provider's actual error detail instead of a bare HTTP status
  (.llm_error_message())
- Retry structured-output calls up to 5x on transient schema/JSON failures
  from Groq, which are not deterministic server-side (.llm_json_retryable())
- Detect systemic failures (auth, 5xx, unreachable endpoint) and emit one
  immediate message() per session, since queued warning()s are invisible
  mid-run and checks would otherwise silently fall back to rules-only
- Fix empty-result edge cases: a 0-row structured response no longer errors
  on join-key assignment; an all-empty response set no longer breaks the
  final left_join
- Reword the summary warning to state how many rows succeeded vs failed

New capabilities:
- On-disk response cache (R/llm-cache.R): llm() runs at temperature 0, so
  identical (model, prompt, text, type, params) calls are deterministic and
  can be replayed from disk instead of re-billing the provider. Controlled
  via llm_cache()/llm_cache_clear()
- llm_max_tokens(): session-wide default so callers do not need to repeat
  params = list(max_tokens = ...) in every module
- llm_reasoning(): session-wide reasoning-effort default, translated per
  model family (gpt-oss, qwen3, Mistral, Ollama each use a different
  mechanism/value set, verified against each provider's actual behaviour).
  Defaults to "low" since every call this package makes is bounded
  extraction/classification, not multi-step reasoning
- vllm/<model> routing via chat_vllm() for custom vLLM endpoints
- phase argument labels the progress bar with the calling step instead of a
  generic "Extracting data"
- llm_model(NULL) now actually clears the model (previously there was no way
  to unset it, since is.null(model) meant "read")

llm() now validates model and params up front, before any network work.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

identically — so they can be replaced by ~1 KB of hashes with no loss except
diff context in the failure message. Purging the existing history requires a
force-push, which per LESSONS L-010 does not clean forks or PR refs.

recent_commits.message: fix(qa): restore the corpus render gate, dead since the 2026-08-06 redaction
recent_commits.body:
`SPIKE_OUT_DIRS` held two identical literals reading "an internal design
doc". The de-referencing pass replaced the two real baseline paths with that
placeholder prose, so every run since printed "ERROR: no spike baselines
found" and exited 1 — while docpluck-qa check 7b documents that exact message
as an expected clean skip on a fresh checkout. A CRITICAL render-regression
gate was disabled for a week and its deadness read as normal. The 26 baseline
files (7 + 19, the documented count) were on disk the whole time.

Resolved via DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR with a runtime default. Missing
fixture is now a loud SKIP (exit 0); baseline dirs that exist but hold no .md
is a FAIL (exit 1). Conflating those two is what trained people to ignore the
message — the same SKIP-vs-ERROR confusion already fixed once in
tests/test_canary_provenance.py.

Restored and run: 26 / 26 PASS at v2.4.126, so this release introduces no
render regression.

recent_commits.message: fix: act on the final verification pass; package is now lint-clean
recent_commits.body:
An independent pass re-derived all eight behavioural claims in fresh
processes against a real paper (identical version dict before vs after
importing every engine; 245ms/16ms; byte-identical default render at
21776 chars vs standard 21777 and none 22487; 12/12 CLI sections carrying
subheadings; zero bare "pdftotext" literals). All eight held. It also found
what follows.

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_v2.4.126.md contained a FALSE claim: "both consumer
surfaces now derive from the dataclass" was true of the library CLI and
false of the service, which still hand-enumerated nine keys and still
dropped `subheadings`. Fixed the data loss rather than only the sentence —
`Section.subheadings` has existed since sectioning v1.6.1, so the service
can emit it against the CURRENT 2.4.125 pin; the switch to Section.to_dict()
stays queued for after the bump. API.md's schema gains the key, and its
`pages` row no longer implies PDF populates it (nothing does).

Three code defects, each reproduced first:
- batch.py imported `fields` and never used it.
- sections/__init__.py annotated `normalization_level` with a forward ref to
  a name imported only inside the function body, so
  typing.get_type_hints(extract_sections) raised NameError. Module-level
  import; verified no cycle (normalize's back-import is lazy, and importing
  docpluck.sections first in a fresh process resolves).
- an unused import in the test module.

Then the lint the sweep implied, all pre-existing: three unused locals
INSPECTED rather than deleted (an assigned-but-unused value in extraction
logic is the "silently dropped computed value" class — all three were
vestigial, none was a lost value), one dead local in SectionedDocument.all()
removed after verifying every documented case still resolves, and four
unused imports. `ruff --select F401,F811,F841` now passes clean over
docpluck/.

Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed, md5-verified against the tested tree.

recent_commits.message: fix(provenance): four surfaces claimed what the call graph did not do
recent_commits.body:
Second, max-effort pass over the v2.4.126 work. The first pass fixed the
reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and
three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in
the code. Full suite 2061 passed / 0 failed (2015 baseline + 46 new).

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also
reports pdftotext_path (the exact binary, resolved once and used by the
extraction call sites too, so the receipt cannot name a build that did not
run), pdfminer.six, pypdfium2, opencv, mammoth, beautifulsoup4, lxml --
two of three input formats were unpinned entirely -- plus python_version
and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

recent_commits.message: feat(provenance): report every input that can change output (v2.4.126)
recent_commits.body:
MetaESCI asks A-1/A-2. A docpluck SHA did not pin extraction: the same SHA
(a5c02ef) against the same PDF (10.1098/rsos.202336) produced 49,091 vs
50,101 normalized chars across a poppler binary replacement, and
get_version_info() reported three keys that were identical in both runs.

Fixes the class, not the symptom. get_version_info() now reports the
pdftotext binary version AND engine (poppler/xpdf differ behaviourally and
share a banner), poppler_version, pdfplumber, camelot, plus the in-repo
sectioning_version and table_extraction_version that were exported and
bumped independently of the package version but never on the receipt.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION is now exported from the package top level.

ExtractionReport carries the same; ExtractionFileResult gains
n_replacement_chars and n_greek_chars (A-2), measured on the normalized
output.

Sibling defects found by sweeping for the same shape:
- NormalizationReport.to_dict() was silently dropping
  column_interleave_pages, a populated field extract_columns documents as
  the canonical source of that signal. Live, predates this change.
- The per-file sidecar recorded ok:false on every SUCCESSFUL extraction,
  and an elapsed_seconds:0.0 written before the timer stopped.
All three hand-enumerated serializers now derive from asdict().

Also: INBOX_* was missing from .gitignore's cross-project correspondence
block, so an inbox doc had been committed to this public repo (unpushed;
those commits were dropped). Duplicate L-010 heading renumbered.

31 tests, all verified failing against the unfixed code first. Full suite
2046 passed / 0 failed.
